data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Ownership-based allocation does not inherently suppress cross-cutting explanations; it acts as a heuristic local search that conserves compute, but it introduces a verifiable suppression risk if the owning lineage's vocabulary lacks the primitives required to express the shortest or most accurate solution.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The owning lineage's universal grammar is Turing-complete and contains all rival primitives as derivable theorems, making cross-lineage reference unnecessary in principle.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Rival lineages fail to produce valid or stronger solutions to the assigned problems, indicating that ownership allocation is globally optimal rather than suppressive.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Cross-cutting explanations are systematically generated by a separate meta-level compilation or abstraction process, rendering object-level lineage ownership irrelevant to their discovery.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Allocation by lineage descent restricts the search space to the local basin of attraction of the parent artifact. If the problem requires a primitive outside the owning lineage's universal grammar, the lineage will fail to solve it or will construct a convoluted, inefficient workaround. Suppression occurs only if the system globally discards superior solutions generated by rival lineages that were not granted ownership but possess the necessary primitive. If rival solutions are merely deferred or stored without being adopted, it is a routing inefficiency rather than an epistemic suppression.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
